summary: The lecture details the historical evolution of India's Constituent Assembly, from early demands by the Indian National Congress and the Simon Commission to the Cabinet Mission Plan, the Assembly's composition, key office-bearers, the Drafting Committee under Ambedkar, the adoption and enforcement of the Constitution, and its original features.
points: Gandhi demanded a Constituent Assembly in 1922; INC officially resolved for it in 1934.
Simon Commission (1927) comprised 7 British members with no Indian representation.
Motilal Nehru Committee (1928) produced the Nehru Report – first Indian-drafted constitutional proposal.
Cabinet Mission (1946) with Cripps, Alexander, Pethick-Lawrence devised the Constituent Assembly formation plan.
Constituent Assembly initially had 389 members (292 provincial, 93 princely, 4 chief commissioner) elected by proportional representation.
First meeting 9 Dec 1946; Temporary President Sachchidananda Sinha; Permanent President Dr. Rajendra Prasad elected 11 Dec 1946.
Drafting Committee (7 members) chaired by B.R. Ambedkar appointed 29 Aug 1947; Constitutional Advisor B.N. Rau.
Constitution adopted 26 Nov 1949 (284 signatures); enforced 26 Jan 1950; originally 395 Articles, 22 Parts, 8 Schedules.
Constituent Assembly took 2 years 11 months 18 days; 11 sessions, 166 sitting days; 2473 amendments moved; cost ₹64 lakh.
Original Constitution handwritten by Prem Behari Narain Raizada in Italian calligraphy; preserved in helium-filled cases in Parliament Library.

check.q: Who was the Temporary President of the Constituent Assembly at its first meeting on 9 December 1946?
Which mission proposed the formation of the Constituent Assembly through elections based on the Government of India Act 1935?
How many members originally constituted the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
